Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  October 3, 2024

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on October 3, 2024. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Octavio Padilla - District 2,
  Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Denmon and second by Commissioner Beck that
the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on August 1, 2024, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioner Padilla, Commissioner McLemore
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Anthony Harris reported the following:
Halloween Family Fest – Join the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
for some Halloween fun on Saturday, October 19, from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. The
Halloween Family Fest will be held on the south lawn at Inglewood City Hall and include
pumpkin decorating, costume parade, carnival- style games, face painting, arts and craft,
food trucks, and more! We hope to see you there. Día de los Muertos – Join us for an
unforgettable spectacle of Día de los Muertos celebration. Also known as, “The Day of the
Dead,” Día de los Muertos is the tradition of celebrating and sharing memories of loved
ones who have passed. The event will showcase its rich heritage, from traditional dressed
altars, to music, arts and crafts, vendor booths, a food court, and more! The event will be

held on Saturday, November 2, from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Inglewood Senior Center.
Inglewood Youth Sports League – Youth Sports continue to create positive memories for
young people in the city. Since last reported, the Inglewood Youth Sports League has
completed the spring and summer season fielded 22 teams, had 280 participants, and 25
coaches volunteered their time this season. Five (5) teams were crowned as champions as
the season concluded on Champion Saturday where all teams enjoyed an end of the
season barbeque and received awards. In Season – The excitement continues as we begin
our Inglewood Rams Flag Football season this fall. Registration is through the roof as we
had to add teams to accommodate the interests for this fall. With 24 teams across four (4)
division and 315 players, the I.Y.S.L sports team is ready to roll. Games are played on
Thursday evenings and all day Saturdays. Come out and catch the action! Girls Volleyball
– Inglewood Youth Sports League is proud to partner with P1440 to bring volleyball to the
City of Inglewood through their “Gives Back” program. This program is much more than
volleyball. It will offer an opportunity for 24 girls between the age of 9 -12 years old to
develop a healthy lifestyle by building confidence and positive habits through physical
movement. This program offers a safe space for girls to learn new skills, be introduced to
the fundamental skills of volleyball, teamwork, and communication. In addition,
participants will develop social-emotional learning tools like breath work and journaling.
The goal is for young ladies to leave the program with a toolkit of physical and mental
exercises that lead to healthier life style and a happier-feeling life. Adaptive Sports Now
In Inglewood – our goal of offering inclusive programs becomes a reality as we ventured
into adaptive sports. The City of Champions was proud to partner with Way Finder, San
Gabriel Valley Panthers, and Beep Baseball to bring an exciting sporting event for the
visually impaired to Inglewood. That event occurred on Saturday, September 9 and
included an Introduction to blind baseball complete with Demonstrations and Specific
stations involving pitching, hitting, and bas running. For more information on our
Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez
reported on the following: Median maintenance - City Council approved funding for Park
Administration to request to bid and hire a landscape maintenance contractor. This will
allow our internal staff to focus on the parks and beautification projects. Sports Field
Maintenance - City Council approved money in the budget to hire a professional sports
field maintenance contractor. By collaborating with a contractor that specializes in
maintaining sports fields, we can keep the fields maintained at a top level and reduce
downtime. Rogers Park - two new picnic tables were installed at Rogers Park near the
baseball fields. The Graffiti Abatement hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia reported the
following: Senior Center Operations - Grace Farwell – H.E.L.P (Helping Elderly Live

productively) & USC Chan of School of Occupational Therapy, helping our seniors improve
their ability to do daily tasks and live as independently as possible with presentations on:
   Medication Management – October 4th
   Senior Scams – October 18th
   Fall Prevention – October 25th
   October 3, 2024 – Presentation/Introduction
   October 10, 2024 – Q & A
   October 31, 2024 – Q & A
   Metro - On the Go Program-Presentation
   October 23, 2024
   Aileen Guzman – St. Barnabas Senior Services – Presentation: Disaster Preparedness

On October 7, 2024, the Legal nonprofit Bet Tzedek will return to finalize estate planning
for 45 seniors. On October 23, 2024, we will celebrate quarterly birthdays (August,
September and October) with theme decorations, dancing and cupcakes. Our highlight of
the month will be our Halloween Party with theme decorations, dancing and a costume
contest.
Senior Nutrition - We are serving approximately 450 seniors per week through home
delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals at our Senior Center. We
continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning
Institute, and monthly shelf stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food
Bank. Transportation - Our paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and
the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. We recently hired on a new part
time bus operator who will assist with any potential service gaps for the paratransit bus
service. They start at the end of September 2024 and we hope to have the new part-time
bus operator in service by mid-October 2024. Child and Adult Care Food Program - Starting
October 1, 2024, the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18
years old and under and operates at Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The
program's hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 p.m. - 3:30 p.m.
and snacks from 4:30 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks
per week.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Director, Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Street
Landscaping - (Tree Division) is returning to Parks, Recreation and Community Services
Department effective as of October 1, 2024. The Public Art Program will be transferred
over to the Library Department also effective October 1.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla invited everyone to attend the
Inglewood Little League opening day on Saturday, October 5, at Rogers Park.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at 6:50 p.m.
